scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and to "fix whatever is causing the wrong bills."
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-05).
The majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills carry read_type ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED (E-01).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% vs a 95% target for ~9200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep (E-04).
Dispute ticket response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) despite the volume surge (E-03).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-05), and this is not explained by slow response handling (median 1.6d/p90 2.8d, within 3.0d SLA; E-03) or a tariff change (0 logged changes; E-02, E-07). A measurable contributor is that manual meter-read route completion for ~9200 accounts fell to 88% vs a 95% target in Aug-Sep (E-04), which triggers estimate substitution that generates disputes: 1240 of 3025 disputed bills (41%) carry read_type ESTIMATED (E-01). The remaining 1785 disputed bills (59%, read_type ACTUAL) are not explained by estimate substitution, so the majority of the surge's cause is not yet established from committed evidence.

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: The observed split (1240 ESTIMATED / 1785 ACTUAL, 59% ACTUAL majority) still holds exactly as measured. But E-12 shows the ESTIMATED pool traces to AMI billing-import rejection (read_channel AMI, not manual field reads), so E-01 no longer supports the A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LINK assumption that tied this ESTIMATED minority to the manual route-completion shortfall in E-04.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-03.statement: No tariff change records exist in billing-db.tariff_change_log for the period examined (0 records).

F-04.statement: Across 2440 dispute tickets, median response time was 1.6 days and p90 was 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA.

F-05.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, across 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-06.statement: Monthly dispute volume rose from 610 (Jun-2026) and 590 (Jul-2026) to 1180 (Aug-2026) and 1260 (Sep-2026).

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 allows the utility to request route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

F-08.statement: route-log.lagging_routes lists 14 routes with below-target completion, each with a distinct completion value; sample route R-00 shows 0.70 completion.

F-09.statement: 320 accounts had an ESTIMATED read in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes.

F-10.statement: 1184 AMI read events underlying disputed ESTIMATED bills were received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import validation with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (firmware v4.2).

F-11.statement: 56 AMI read events underlying disputed ESTIMATED bills had no read received before cutoff (status NO_READ_RECEIVED) and were not exported to billing.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: The August-September dispute surge is driven by slow/inadequate ticket response handling (backlog), not by an increase in actually incorrect bills; auto-answering would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August (logged in DA-RULES) is causing reads to be rejected or mis-processed, producing incorrect bills and disputes.

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: A degraded or incomplete AMI read export from the vendor (H-MDMS-BILL handoff) is causing missing/estimated reads that generate wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter-read collection or the daily upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) from MeterWorks has degraded since August, increasing estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-LEGITIMATE-BILL-INCREASE.statement: Bills themselves are correctly computed but disputes rose because of a legitimate tariff/rate or seasonal usage change unrelated to any pipeline defect.

H-ROUTINE-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTIO.statement: A baseline level of estimate substitution occurs across most routes (40 distinct routes with estimated accounts) independent of the staffing-driven route-completion shortfall (only 14 lagging routes), implying another driver also contributes to the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills.

H-AMI-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTI.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), causing estimate substitution for those accounts and accounting for the ESTIMATED-read portion of disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-01 (billing-db, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) splits disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL, so the majority (1785/3025, ~59%) of disputed bills were on ACTUAL (not estimated/substituted) reads. Estimate-substitution-driven theories therefore explain only a minority (~41%) of the disputed bills.

The observed split (1240 ESTIMATED / 1785 ACTUAL, 59% ACTUAL majority) still holds exactly as measured. But E-12 shows the ESTIMATED pool traces to AMI billing-import rejection (read_channel AMI, not manual field reads), so E-01 no longer supports the A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-LINK assumption that tied this ESTIMATED minority to the manual route-completion shortfall in E-04.

E-02 (billing-db, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) shows 0 records in tariff_change_log, meaning no tariff/rate change was logged, which rules out a tariff change as a driver of the bill increases/dispute surge.

E-03 shows CRM ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so response handling itself is not slow despite the ticket volume surge. This undercuts the premise that a response-handling backlog explains the doubling of disputes.

E-04 (route-log, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) shows field route completion for manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. manual meter-read routes ran below their completion target during the dispute-surge window.

The observation that manual-read route completion was 88% vs a 95% target over Aug-Sep across 9200 accounts still holds. But E-12 shows the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-01) are driven by AMI reads rejected/missing at billing import, not by manual field-read non-completion, so E-04 no longer supports the premise that this route-completion shortfall is causing the ESTIMATED-read dispute pool.

E-05 (crm-tickets, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) confirms dispute volume roughly doubled from the Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to Aug (1180) and stayed elevated in Sep (1260), i.e. the surge began in August and has not receded on its own in Sep.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, has an incentive toward contract headcount increase) attributes the below-target route completion (E-04: 88% vs 95%) to being short three meter readers since July, causing late routes and estimated bills for those customers. This is an unverified causal claim consistent with E-04's completion gap but does not itself establish how many disputed bills resulted from these estimated reads.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year, a non-authoritative claim that agrees with the already-established tool finding E-02 (0 records in tariff_change_log). This corroborates, rather than adds new weight to, the existing ruling-out of a tariff change as a dispute driver.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a contract clause confirming the governance mechanism for route priority changes: the utility may request them, but the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) must confirm execution. This corroborates, rather than adds new causal information to, the existing K-DISPATCH authority/approval constraint on push_route_update.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 (route-log, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) breaks the Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (E-04: 88% vs 95%) into 14 individual lagging routes with distinct completion rates (sample R-00 at 0.70), showing the shortfall is spread across multiple routes rather than concentrated in one. It contains no reader-staffing or route-assignment fields, so it does not itself confirm or refute SH-FIELD's reader-staffing-shortage claim (E-06/CL-02).

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-10 (billing-db, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) shows 320 accounts had ESTIMATED reads in the last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes — a wider route footprint than the 14 routes flagged as below-target completion in E-09. This indicates estimate substitution is not confined to the staffing-shortfall-linked lagging routes, weakening the assumed tight link between the measured route-completion shortfall and the full pool of ESTIMATED disputed bills.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, NOT_APPLICABLE completeness) reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside was provisioned today per vendor ticket TX-4471, which, if accurate, would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export:read_events_for_disputed_estimated query. This is a claim about access/provisioning status only; it contains no AMI read-event data and asserts nothing about billing causes.

All records are read_channel AMI, not manual field reads, so this ESTIMATED-bill pool traces to AMI/billing-import rejection, not to the manual route-completion shortfall (E-04) previously assumed to link to it.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.question: Did a billing import validation rule change in DA-RULES around August cause reads to be rejected or mis-processed on ACTUAL-read bills, producing the majority of disputes?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Resolves whether the majority (59%) of disputed ACTUAL-read bills are caused by a rule change, which determines whether any bill-correction or rule-reversion response is warranted.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query billing-config.billing_import_validation_rule_change_log for change records and dates, and correlate with the onset/composition of ACTUAL-read disputed bills.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Continue diagnostic investigation only; take no bill-correction or rule-reversion action until the rule-change log is queried and a cause is evidenced.

U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.question: Is the route completion shortfall actually caused by being short three readers since July (SH-FIELD's claim, E-06, non-authoritative with a headcount incentive), or by another field-ops factor?
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.decision_impact: Determines whether any route-priority change (push_route_update) should target a staffing-driven cause or a different field-ops factor.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.resolution_path: Cross-check SH-FIELD's staffing claim against field-dispatch roster/assignment records independent of SH-FIELD's own report.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-VERIFICATI.safe_placeholder: Do not execute push_route_update based on the staffing claim alone; keep route monitoring active pending independent verification.

U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.question: Is the 2-month Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month, E-05) representative and non-seasonal for the 'back to baseline' success target, or could seasonal variation shift the expected Aug-Sep volume?
U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.decision_impact: Affects whether the SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-NORMALIZED threshold (<=700/month) is a valid success target or needs seasonal adjustment.
U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.resolution_path: Extend crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly history to prior years to check for seasonal patterns around Aug-Sep.
U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.safe_placeholder: Report dispute volume trend against the current baseline while flagging it as provisional pending longer-history confirmation.

U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-FIELD-BILL daily manual-read upload handoff from MeterWorks reliably delivered and semantically valid, or is handoff degradation (beyond the measured route-completion shortfall) also contributing to estimate substitution?
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Determines whether the H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE hypothesis requires handoff-specific remediation scope beyond route-completion monitoring.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Check H-FIELD-BILL delivery logs and payload validation records to establish its delivery_status and semantic_validity, currently UNKNOWN.
U-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Continue monitor_route_completion as the diagnostic scope; do not assert handoff failure as a confirmed cause until delivery/semantic validity is checked.

hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-CS's framing (SH-CS potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem) and determines whether a chatbot-style fix is even relevant versus a billing-pipeline fix; K-BILLWRITE also blocks any automated bill-write remedy regardless.

hypotheses.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August (logged in DA-RULES) is causing reads to be rejected or mis-processed, producing incorrect bills and disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If a rule change is the cause, the fix is a config rollback/correction in ORG-UTIL's billing system, constrained by K-BILLWRITE (no automated bill writes) and requiring SH-BILL authority, not an AI ticket agent.
discriminating_evidence: DA-RULES (validation rule change log timing vs August)
DA-BILL (read-type/estimate ratios before vs after August)

hypotheses.rationale: This would implicate ORG-AMI's vendor pipeline (DA-MDMS) rather than CS tooling, requiring vendor-provisioned export access (noted acquisition constraint on DA-MDMS) and coordination with SH-AMI.
discriminating_evidence: DA-MDMS vs DA-BILL (accepted AMI reads vs billed reads reconciliation)

hypotheses.statement: Manual meter-read collection or the daily upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) from MeterWorks has degraded since August, increasing estimate substitution and billing errors.
hypotheses.rationale: SH-FIELD has a noted incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing), so this hypothesis must be tested against route-completion data rather than accepted on SH-FIELD's framing.

hypotheses.statement: Bills themselves are correctly computed but disputes rose because of a legitimate tariff/rate or seasonal usage change unrelated to any pipeline defect.
hypotheses.rationale: If true, no technical pipeline fix is needed at all; the appropriate response is communication/explanation to customers, which is a very different intervention than fixing billing data flows.
